To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thermopower in the asymmetric cell, Ag ¦ α - AgI ¦ Ag 2S, is equal to that in the symmetric one, Ag ¦ α- AgI ¦ Ag, and that the transported entropy of metallic Ag in α-AgI is equal to the standard molar entropy of metallic Ag, S 0 = 41.2 J mol-1 K-1.

(1) The thermopower of a symmetric cell is equal to the sum of the thermopower contributions of its two electrodes; and (2) The thermopowers of the electrolyte and of its electrodes in an asymmetric cell are not additive.
the thermopower in an asymmetric cell involving a mixed conductor as a probe electrode can be measured in a stationary state and is related to the standard entropy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to measuring the thermopower (or the entropy transport) of an electrolyte.
the study of thermoelectric phenomena in asymmetric cells involving mixed conductors.
the thermoelectric effects in a solid state electrolyte with the common ion effect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a mixed conductor can be used as an effective information transmitter for the thermopower measurements of electrolytes under the Soret condition.

the thermopower measurements on the asymmetric thermocell involving a mixed conductor as a probe electrode provide the information on the entropy of transport of the ions in a solid electrolyte under equilibrium conditions.
the thermopower measurements of the asymmetric thermocell involving a mixed conductor probe are useful for studying the thermodynamic properties of the mixed conductor and the electrolyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermopower measurements of electrolytes are feasible by using a mixed conductor as a probe electrode.
the mixed conductor electrode can be used for the determination of the thermopower in a system involving a mixed conductor.
the asymmetric cell, Ag ¦ α -AgI ¦ Ag2S, is capable of providing information on the thermopower and the entropy of transport of Ag in AgI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymmetric cell with the mixed conductor probe is an efficient tool for studying the thermopower in electrolytes.
the asymmetric cell can serve as a tool for the study of thermoelectricity of the electrolytes with common ions.
the thermopower measurements can be used as a probe for the entropy of ions in the electrolyte.
